editorial:
Imagine you are a publisher whose entire business depends on one writer, but there is a huge catch: she can only write when she is miserable. You get to follow the chaotic journey of a man who has to purposefully make a woman sad just to save his career. It is a quirky, lighthearted ride that plays with the idea of love and pain. The vibe is very sweet and a bit silly, making it the kind of movie you put on when you just want to relax and smile. You will find yourself rooting for them even though their relationship starts on a pretty weird foundation.

The acting is charming and the pacing keeps things moving quickly so you never get bored. While the plot is a bit predictable, the chemistry between the leads makes it work. If you enjoy rom-coms that do not take themselves too seriously, you will love this one.
endingExplained: After spending the movie trying to make her sad, the publisher realizes he actually loves her. He stops the games and tells her the truth about his plan. Even though she is upset at first, they decide to be together. The twist is that she discovers she can actually write great stories while being happy, proving that misery is not the only way to be creative. They end up as a happy couple in both life and work.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves cute romantic comedies with a twist.
